7 "intent": "A normative typographic specification for printed documents — essays, letters, reports. This file is the source of truth. CSS, Typst, LaTeX or any other implementation conforms to it; where an implementation and this file disagree, this file is right.",
8 "target": "Paper and PDF at 100% scale. Not screens, not reflowing layouts.",
9 "conformance": [
10 "Every length is absolute. Points (pt) and millimetres (mm) mean the same thing in every engine; 1pt = 1/72in.",
11 "A length given in em is relative to the font size of the element it is declared on, not to the document base.",
12 "line_height is a multiple of the element's own font size, and defines the baseline-to-baseline advance. An engine whose leading is measured between line boxes rather than between baselines must derive its value from the resulting advance, stated per element in baseline_advance.",
13 "An implementation MUST reproduce every value under `properties`. It MAY add anything the target engine needs to achieve them.",
14 "Where an engine cannot express a property, it must fail visibly or degrade as named in `fallback` — never silently.",
15 "Colour is sRGB. Ink is never pure black: #000 blooms on laser output and glares in a backlit PDF.",
16 "Deriving leading: where the engine measures the gap between line boxes rather than between baselines, pin the line box to the band from the baseline up to 1em (in Typst: top-edge: 1em, bottom-edge: 0pt). The advance is then 1em + leading, so leading = (line_height - 1) em, independent of the font's own metrics."
17 ],

53 "note": "Symmetric is what a document gets unless it asks otherwise: the named size applies to all four sides. Duplex is the explicit opt-in, for a sheet that will be bound — top and bottom stay at the symmetric value, and left and right split into an inner (binding) edge and an outer edge. A duplex pair preserves its symmetric pair's total, inner plus outer equal to twice the symmetric value, and shifts the gutter by 3mm: 20+20=40 becomes 23+17. A document keeps the same text width whichever it chooses, so switching between symmetric and duplex never reflows it."
54 },
55 "text_width": "Not a stated constant: the paper width minus the left and right margins — twice the symmetric value, or inner plus outer for a duplex pair. The two are equal for any one size, by the rule above.",

211 "title": "Headings",
212 "group": "Structure",
213 "principles": [
214 "Sans against the serif body, so hierarchy reads by contrast rather than by size alone.",
215 "Below level 4 the size stops changing and the register shifts instead — small caps, then italic. Six distinct levels inside a 24pt–11pt range.",
216 "Space above is four times the space below: a heading belongs to what follows it.",
217 "A heading MUST NOT be the last thing on a page. This is the most common defect in printed documents."

374 "title": "Paragraphs",
375 "group": "Prose",
376 "principles": [
377 "Two conventions, one switch. Spaced paragraphs suit documents that get skimmed. Indented paragraphs with no gap suit continuous prose and are the convention of nearly every printed book.",
378 "The first paragraph after any heading, block or break is flush left: the thing above it has already marked the start."

414 {
415 "id": "justification",
416 "title": "Alignment: ragged or justified",
417 "group": "Prose",
418 "opt_in": "typeset--justified",
419 "principles": [
420 "Ragged right is the DEFAULT, and it is a choice rather than an absence — a document states it. Justification buys a clean right edge at the cost of uneven word spacing; a ragged setting keeps the spacing even and gives up the edge. Neither is more correct, but the cost lands differently by document.",
421 "Choose ragged right for a letter, a memorandum, a short note — anything addressed to a person rather than to a readership. Justification reads as institutional, and its even edge is the visual signature of print that was set for strangers.",
422 "Choose justification for continuous prose at a full measure: an essay, a report, a paper. It is mandatory in two columns, where a ragged edge at 50 characters serrates the column.",
423 "These are a single decision. Justification without hyphenation opens rivers of white space; hyphenation without justification breaks words for no gain. Take both or neither.",
424 "Hyphenation is per-language and requires the document language to be declared. An English dictionary applied to Portuguese produces confident nonsense.",
425 "The last line of a paragraph is NEVER stretched. State this explicitly — a paginating engine fragments the text, so the visual last line stops looking like the end of a paragraph and gets justified. It does not reproduce in an unpaginated preview.",
426 "Justification applies to prose only. It MUST NOT reach a subtitle, byline, caption, address block, table cell, heading or listing. In an engine where alignment inherits, every such block declares its own alignment rather than relying on an exception list.",
427 "Alignment inherits, and so does last-line alignment. A block that sets its own alignment — a centred pull quote, a centred section break — must also set its own last-line alignment, or the document's justification flushes its last line (its only line, for a one-liner) to the left."
428 ],
429 "elements": [
430 {
431 "id": "justification-ragged",
432 "name": "Ragged right (default)",
433 "opt_in": "typeset--ragged — names the default; no class needed to get it",
434 "properties": {
435 "align": "left",
436 "align_last_line": "left",
437 "hyphenation": "manual — never automatic",
438 "line_breaking": "high effort: avoid a very short last line, and even out the right edge",
439 "applies_to": [
440 "paragraph",
441 "list item",
442 "blockquote",
443 "definition description",
444 "callout"
445 ]
446 },
447 "notes": [
448 "Hyphenation exists to serve justification. Without justification a hyphen breaks a word for no gain, so it stays off.",
449 "The rag itself is the thing to judge: an even rag reads as deliberate, a rag with one very short line and one very long one reads as an accident."
450 ]

777 "id": "quotes",
778 "title": "Quotations",
779 "group": "Blocks",
780 "principles": [
781 "Four jobs, four treatments. A block quote is evidence. An epigraph opens a chapter. A pull quote is display type lifted from the body. Verse preserves the poet's line breaks.",
782 "A pull quote repeats text that already appears in the body, so it MUST NOT be the only place a claim appears — a skimming reader would get the claim without its qualification.",
783 "Attribution always sits outside the quotation. Inside, it becomes part of what was said."

964 "principles": [
965 "Rules, not grids. Vertical rules are almost never needed — the columns already read as columns, and every added line is ink competing with data.",

968 "Numbers align on their right edge, on tabular figures. Units go in the header, not in every cell.",

1196 "group": "Blocks",
1197 "principles": [
1198 "A blank line cannot survive a page break: if the break falls on the gap, the reader never learns the scene changed. Over a long document this is a certainty, not an accident. The mark MUST be visible.",
1199 "Four registers, one per kind of division."

1258 {
1259 "id": "notes",
1260 "title": "Footnotes, endnotes & sidenotes",
1261 "group": "Apparatus",
1262 "principles": [
1263 "Bottom-of-page footnotes require an engine that can measure the page while laying it out. Typst and LaTeX do this natively. WeasyPrint 53+ and Prince implement the CSS footnote model. No browser does.",
1264 "Where footnotes are unavailable the note text MUST still live in the document, degrading to a numbered endnotes block — never to a lost note.",
1265 "Sidenotes are the better default where the page can afford the margin: no page-break arithmetic, and the reader never leaves the sentence they are in.",
1266 "The reference mark must not disturb the leading of the line it sits on."
1267 ],
1268 "elements": [

1270 "id": "notes-marker",
1271 "name": "Reference mark",
1272 "properties": {

1277 "color": "accent",

1282 }

1288 "position": "foot of the page carrying the mark",
1289 "font": "serif",
1290 "size": "9.5pt",
1291 "line_height": 1.35,
1292 "separator": "a rule above the notes area"
1293 },
1294 "fallback": "an endnotes block at the end of the document"
1295 },
1296 {
1297 "id": "notes-endnotes",
1298 "name": "Endnotes block",
1299 "properties": {
1300 "font": "serif",
1301 "size": "9.5pt",
1302 "line_height": 1.4,
1303 "align": "left",
1304 "space_before": "22pt",
1305 "border_top": "0.5pt rule",
1306 "padding_top": "11pt",
1307 "list_indent": "1.8em",
1308 "item_space_after": "0.4em",
1309 "heading": "none — the rule above the block is the only mark it needs"
1310 },
1311 "notes": [
1312 "No 'NOTES' label. In a one-page document the rule plus the numbered list already reads as a notes area, and a heading over two lines of small print is heavier than the thing it labels."
1313 ]
1314 },
1315 {
1316 "id": "notes-sidenote",
1317 "name": "Sidenote",
1318 "opt_in": "typeset--sidenotes",
1319 "properties": {
1320 "font": "sans",
1321 "size": "8pt",
1322 "line_height": 1.4,
1323 "color": "ink_muted",
1324 "align": "left",
1325 "width": "11em",
1326 "position": "the right margin, 2em past the text column's own right edge",
1327 "vertical_offset": "-0.3em from the marker's line",
1328 "marker_prefix": "the note number in accent, weight 600",
1329 "measure_when_active": "27em",
1330 "reserved_margin": "14em — the gap plus the note, with an em to spare"
1331 },
1332 "notes": [
1333 "Anchor the note to the text column's right edge, not to the measure. The measure is a maximum: where the reserved margin is the binding constraint the column is narrower than it, and a note offset from the measure lands on top of the text.",
1334 "Sidenotes are positioned, not flowed: a long note followed closely by another will overlap it. Keep each note short and consecutive notes apart — one per paragraph, and not in every paragraph. An implementation cannot fix this, and should not pretend to; it is a constraint on the writing."
1335 ]
1336 }
1337 ]

1508 {
1509 "id": "letter",
1510 "title": "Letter",
1511 "group": "Documents",
1512 "principles": [
1513 "A letter is set ragged right. It is addressed to a person, and justification reads as institutional.",
1514 "The sender block is address data, not a masthead: one style throughout, at body size, in the reading face. Nothing bold, nothing in the sans. A personal letter does not announce itself.",
1515 "Address blocks are line-broken data, not prose: tighter leading, never justified, line breaks as authored.",
1516 "The signature is the typed name with room above it to sign. No ruled line — a rule is a form to be filled in.",
1517 "A letter carries no running head and no folio.",
1518 "Footnotes belong in a letter as much as in an essay. Where the engine cannot set them at the page foot, the rule plus the numbered note at the end of a one-page letter reads as a footnote area regardless."
1519 ],
1520 "elements": [
1521 {
1522 "id": "letter-page",
1523 "name": "Letter page",
1524 "properties": {

1683 "The small set of overrides reached for while proofing a real document. Every one of them is a manual decision about a specific page, not a style."
1684 ],

1753 "templates": {
1754 "default": "single-column",
1755 "note": "A template sets the page and the scale. Everything under `foundation` and `sections` still applies; a template states only what it overrides, and what it forbids.",
1756 "single-column": {
1757 "name": "Single column",
1758 "use_for": "Essays, letters, reports, memoranda — anything read continuously from start to finish.",
1759 "page": "as foundation.page",
1760 "scale": "as foundation.scale",
1761 "rhythm": "as foundation.rhythm",
1762 "justification": "optional",
1763 "notes": [
1764 "The default. Nothing to opt into."
1765 ]
1766 },
1767 "two-column": {
1768 "name": "Two column, equal",
1769 "opt_in": "typeset--two-column",
1770 "use_for": "Papers, journal articles, newsletters, technical notes — documents that are scanned and referenced as much as read, and where a figure is worth more than an uninterrupted argument.",
1771 "derivation": {
1772 "derived_for": "The paper named in foundation.page.size, at the margin named in foundation.page.margins.default. No copy of either is kept here: every number below is a function of those two and of the gutter.",
1773 "column_gap_mm": 6,
1774 "column_width_mm": 82,
1775 "characters_per_line": {
1776 "11pt": 43,
1777 "10.5pt": 45,
1778 "10pt": 47,
1779 "9.5pt": 50,
1780 "9pt": 52
1781 },
1782 "floor": 45,
1783 "margins_supported": [
1784 "narrow",
1785 "standard"
1786 ],
1787 "conclusion": "An 82mm column carries 43 characters at the 11pt base — below the 45-character floor this spec sets for a line of prose. The base size therefore DROPS to 9.5pt, which gives 50. 10.5pt reaches 45 exactly, and a floor is not a target: 9.5pt is the first step with room above it. This is arithmetic, not preference: an implementation that keeps 11pt in two columns violates the measure rule, which is the rule everything else in this spec is downstream of.",
1788 "refusal": "Two columns are refused, not set badly, on any paper and margin whose column falls below the floor. That is a computed rule rather than a list of papers: margins_supported names the margins that reach the floor on the paper in foundation.page.size, and tools/check.mjs recomputes it. The checker fails when this declaration disagrees with the arithmetic, when the default margin cannot reach the floor, or when no named margin on the paper can.",
1789 "recompute_when": "The paper in foundation.page.size, the default margin, or the gutter. Characters per line = (foundation.rhythm.measure_chars / measure_mm) x column_mm x (11 / base_pt), rounded; column_mm = (paper width - twice the margin - the gutter) / 2. tools/check.mjs recomputes every number here from foundation.page, so a margin cannot move without these following it or the checker going red."
1790 },
1791 "page": {
1792 "size": "as foundation.page.size",
1793 "margins": "as foundation.page.margins, at the default size — symmetric unless the sheet is bound, duplex if it is. A duplex pair leaves the text width unchanged, so a two-column document does not reflow between them.",
1794 "columns": 2,
1795 "column_widths": "equal — the two columns are the same width, always",
1796 "column_gap_mm": 6,
1797 "column_width_mm": 82,
1798 "column_rule": "none by default; an optional 0.5pt hairline in `rule` where the columns need separating",
1799 "column_balance": "the final page balances its columns to equal height",
1800 "lines_per_column": 54,
1801 "running_head": "as foundation.page — spans the full text width, not a column",
1802 "folio": "as foundation.page"
1803 },
1804 "scale": {
1805 "ratio": 1.2,
1806 "base": "9.5pt",
1807 "steps": {
1808 "xs": "7pt",
1809 "sm": "8.5pt",
1810 "base": "9.5pt",
1811 "h4": "9.5pt",
1812 "h3": "11pt",
1813 "h2": "13pt",
1814 "h1": "20pt"
1815 },
1816 "note": "Every step comes down. A 24pt heading inside an 82mm column takes three lines to say two words; 18pt takes two. The h1 keeps display size because it spans both columns."
1817 },
1818 "rhythm": {
1819 "line_height": 1.4,
1820 "baseline_advance": "13.3pt",
1821 "space": "9.5pt",
1822 "measure": "the column — 82mm, not a character count",
1823 "measure_chars": 50,
1824 "note": "Leading tightens with the measure: a shorter line needs less vertical separation to keep the return sweep unambiguous."
1825 },
1826 "requirements": [
1827 "Justification with hyphenation is MANDATORY, not optional. At 50 characters a ragged right edge produces a visibly serrated column and word gaps wide enough to read as rivers. This is the one place the spec removes a choice it otherwise offers.",
1828 "The last line of a paragraph is still flush left. Two columns make a stretched last line more visible, not less.",
1829 "Balance the columns on the final page. A last page with one full column and one empty third reads as a printing error.",
1830 "A spanning element must span BOTH columns fully or neither. An element that spans one and a half columns has no correct reading order.",
1831 "Keep a spanning element at the top or the bottom of the page, never mid-column. Interrupting both columns in the middle forces the reader to find their place twice."
1832 ],
1833 "spanning": {
1834 "always": [
1835 "frontmatter-title-block",
1836 "frontmatter-subtitle",
1837 "frontmatter-byline",
1838 "frontmatter-dateline",
1839 "frontmatter-abstract",
1840 "headings-h1",
1841 "frontmatter-colophon"
1842 ],
1843 "optional": [
1844 "figure",
1845 "table",
1846 "code block",
1847 "pull quote"
1848 ],
1849 "never": [
1850 "paragraph",
1851 "list",
1852 "blockquote",
1853 "callout",
1854 "heading 2 and below",
1855 "endnotes"
1856 ],
1857 "note": "A wide figure or table opts in per instance. The default is column-width, because a spanning element costs a break in both columns. `always` is element ids, so tools/check.mjs can hold both implementations to it; `optional` and `never` stay prose because they describe author choice and default flow, which nothing enforces. A bibliography heading is not on `always`: no heading element exists anywhere in this spec, and the bibliography section's own element list carries none either."
1858 },
1859 "forbidden": {
1860 "sidenote": "There is no margin to put it in. Use a footnote or an endnote.",
1861 "dropcap": "A three-line cap at 3.05em is 29pt in an 82mm column — 10mm of the column given to one letter. Open with small caps instead.",
1862 "measure_variants": "narrow and wide are meaningless: the column is the measure."
1863 },
